title: ASML Raises Full-Year Sales Outlook as AI Boom Drives Demand
source_used: Bloomberg (opening paragraphs, paywalled) and Anadolu Agency's full report of ASML's results
key_facts: ASML Holding NV raised its 2026 sales forecast on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 (Bloomberg); Anadolu gives the new range as €44 billion to €45 billion against €43 billion to €45 billion before.
ASML said its current supply plans mean it cannot fully meet demand in 2027 and 2028; it is looking at raising 2028 capacity beyond the 30% increase previously communicated.
Chief executive Christophe Fouquet: 'Customers are asking us every single day to get more tools.'
Third-quarter net profit was €4.96 billion ($5.55 billion), above analysts' expectations; net sales of €11.66 billion were slightly below expectations (Anadolu).
Fourth-quarter net sales are projected at €14.2 billion to €15.2 billion; some customers have expressed interest in orders for 2029 and 2030 (Anadolu).
ASML is the world's sole producer of extreme ultraviolet lithography machines; it kept its forecast that China would be 20% of sales and faces export limits on EUV machines to China (Anadolu).
quote_evidence: ASML said its current supply plans mean it won't be able to fully meet demand in 2027 and 2028.
ASML now expects annual net sales of €44 billion to €45 billion, compared with its previous forecast of €43 billion to €45 billion.
Some customers were expressing interest in placing orders for 2029 and even 2030, he said, indicating demand visibility extending beyond the next few years.
why_it_matters_hint: The sole maker of the machines behind advanced chips says AI demand will exceed its supply for two years.
notes: Bloomberg text in the prefetch holds only the first two paragraphs (paywall); the figures were read in Anadolu Agency's full report (aa.com.tr). CNBC's page was blocked (Akamai). Some outlets headline a falling share price after the results (Yahoo Finance, Invezz); that is not used because it was not read. The Bloomberg lead says ASML 'boosted its own 2026 sales forecast'; Anadolu says it raised the lower end of the range.
